chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abū Usāmah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a junub who sweats in his garment, or who performs ghusl and then embraces his wife and lies with her while she is menstruating or junub, and some of her sweat touches his body. He said: “All of this is of no consequence.”

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: is of no consequence; not legally significant here
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a junub or a menstruating woman make the body or clothing impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and contact with sweat in states of janabah and menstruation. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such contact is not considered anything consequential, indicating that it does not render the body or clothing impure in this case.
